title: The Existence of a Neutron (Chadwick, 1932)
summary: In 1932 James Chadwick published in Proceedings of the Royal Society A a peer-reviewed paper, The Existence of a Neutron, reporting the proof of a neutral particle with about the same mass as a proton.
body: James Chadwick, then at Cambridge, published the paper The Existence of a Neutron in Proceedings of the Royal Society of London, Series A, volume 136, pages 692-708, registered under DOI 10.1098/rspa.1932.0112, with the Crossref-issued date 1932-06-01 [1]. The INSPIRE-HEP bibliographic record lists it as a refereed, citeable 17-page article by Chadwick, J., affiliated with Cambridge U., with the title taken from CrossRef [2]. In 1932, Chadwick proved that the penetrating radiation earlier produced by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles consisted of a neutral particle with about the same mass as a proton, a particle earlier hypothesised by Ernest Rutherford to exist in atomic nuclei [3]. Chadwick was awarded the 1935 Nobel Prize in Physics, with prize motivation cited as for the discovery of the neutron [3].
